approach: Fault: `write_checkpoint` (attribution.rs:727) calls `RecordsWriter::append`, which writes only the local `athena/records` ref. The next `append_to_remote` (landing, via `sync_from`, records_branch.rs:374) resets the local ref to the remote tip, so the unpushed checkpoint is dropped and CI never finds one. Fix at that call. `write_checkpoint` takes a remote name and does two things. First it fetches the remote records tip and refuses (an `Err` string, so `checkpoint_error`) if the remote has no records branch or the records tip the check judged is not an ancestor of the remote tip. Without this guard the sync would silently discard unpushed local records and the checkpoint's `records_sha` would name a commit the remote lacks. Then it calls `RecordsWriter::append_to_remote(remote, "checkpoint", ...)`, which already does sync, compare-and-swap push (`push_if_remote_at`), rebuild-and-retry up to 8 attempts, and `Contended`. `Options` gains a `remote` field (default `"origin"`, the literal `land_pr` uses at gh/landing.rs:743) so both callers (`check --attribution`, `checkpoint_after_landing`) reach the remote with no signature change to `Options::new`. A failed push stays `checkpoint_error` and the verdict is kept. The existing tests write records locally and then expect checkpoints, so they get a bare `origin` and a `publish` helper (a plain, non-forced `push_branch` of the local records tip, as test setup). The new tests read the bare remote directly. `crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs` is not touched (gh/ is a directory; the remote literal already exists there).

decisions.choice: Guard in write_checkpoint: the judged records tip must be an ancestor of the fetched remote tip, else return an error string (no write).
decisions.reason: `append_to_remote` first resets the local branch to the remote. If local were ahead (records never pushed), those commits would be lost and the checkpoint's `records_sha` would name a commit the remote lacks, so every later incremental run would fall back at attribution.rs:627-637. If the judged tip is an ancestor, nothing is lost and a remote that moved ahead is fine, because the checkpoint is built on the newer tip with the older `records_sha` and the next run judges the records in between. The remote only moves by fast-forward, so the ancestry still holds at push time.

risks.risk: A developer clone whose local `athena/records` is ahead of the remote (an unpushed landing record) now writes no checkpoint, where before it wrote a local one.
risks.mitigation: The guard returns a `checkpoint_error` string and writes nothing. The next check (after the records are pushed or fetched) writes the checkpoint. The error text names the judged tip and the remote.

risks.risk: If the push succeeds but the local `set_ref` then fails (records_branch.rs:445), the run reports an error although the remote has the checkpoint.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: `checkpoint_error` is set and the checkpoint is on the remote, so the next `sync_from` realigns the local ref. The changelog and doc comment say the local ref is updated after a successful push. A test of this edge is not added.

risks.risk: Adapting about seven existing gate tests to a bare remote may break a count or parent assertion, and per-record pushes in the 200-landing timing test would be slow.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 keeps `publish` as a plain, non-forced push, so a non-fast-forward test setup fails loudly. The 200-landing test keeps local puts and publishes once.

risks.risk: A repo with no `origin` (or one only readable) now cannot write a checkpoint.
risks.mitigation: The error is reported as `checkpoint_error` with the git message, and the verdict and exit code are unchanged. `athena land` prints the note to stderr only.

risks.risk: Checkpoints already written locally (for example 5c314d0) were dropped by earlier resets; the fix does not recover them.
risks.mitigation: The changelog entry says checkpoints are never retroactively pushed. A maintainer's next passing check on main writes a new one, and the weekly full replay still runs.

demonstrations.method: New unit test `attribution::tests::checkpoint_reaches_the_remote_records_branch`. Build a repo with a bare `origin` (a helper `add_remote(&git)` that runs `init --bare` and `remote add origin <path>`), land two commits with `land()`, call `publish(&git)`, then run `run_check(&git, &head, now(), &incremental())`. Read the bare repo directly: `bare.rev_parse(RECORDS_REF)` equals the local tip and `bare.show_file(remote_tip, "checkpoints/<cp.id>.json")` parses to `HistoryRecord::Checkpoint(cp)` with `main_sha` = head and `records_sha` = the tip before the write. The remote tip's only parent is the old tip.
demonstrations.observes: The checkpoint file exists on the bare remote's `athena/records` tip, read from the remote and not the local ref. `run.checkpoint_written` is Some and `checkpoint_error` is None.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `RecordsWriter::append` the bare remote has no `checkpoints/` file and the show_file/remote-tip assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: New test `attribution::tests::a_later_landing_fast_forwards_past_the_remote_checkpoint`. After the criterion-1 setup, write a landing record through the production writer: `RecordsWriter::new(&git).append_to_remote("origin", "landing", &[Change::put("landings/x.json", ..)], &[])`. Read the bare remote: `checkpoints/<cp.id>.json` is still in the tip's tree, `bare.is_ancestor(checkpoint_commit, new_tip)` is true, `git.parents(new_tip) == [checkpoint_commit]`, and `audit_history(&bare, new_tip)` is empty. Also assert the local ref equals the remote tip (not reset).
demonstrations.observes: The remote tip descends from the checkpoint commit with the checkpoint file intact, and nothing was reset.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old local `append`, `append_to_remote`'s `sync_from` resets the local ref to the remote tip, the checkpoint file is absent from the remote, and the file-present assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `run_check` then `RecordsWriter::append_to_remote`, which exists (records_branch.rs:398). The fixture is the bare `origin` from `add_remote` (step 5). The checkpoint commit id is the return of the check's remote tip read right after `run_check`.

demonstrations.method: New test `attribution::tests::ci_incremental_run_from_the_remote_checkpoint_judges_only_later_commits`. Land 3 commits and check them (checkpoint pushed). Land 2 more with the landing records written by `append_to_remote`. Simulate CI's fresh state: `git update-ref -d refs/heads/athena/records`, then `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records` (the same fetch ci.yml:646 runs). Run `run_check(&git, &head, now(), &Options::new(Mode::Incremental, false))`. Assert `mode == Incremental`, `started_from.main_sha` equals the third commit, `commits_judged() == 2`, `records_judged() == 4` (checkpoints are excluded at attribution.rs:338), and `fallback_reason` is None. A second run on the same repo with the checkpoint absent (a control remote with no checkpoint) is a full replay of 5 commits.
demonstrations.observes: The incremental run starts from the checkpoint that came from the remote and judges only the two later commits and their four records, not all five.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the push, the fetched local ref has no checkpoint, so `mode` is FullReplay, `fallback_reason` is "no checkpoint on the records branch" and `commits_judged` is 5, which fails the assertions.
